ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a fused bicyclic organic structure, with a benzene ring on the left, and the right side fused with it to form a second six-membered ring. At the upper right there is an external C=N–NH2+ fragment, and at the lower right a six-membered-ring carbon is connected to a substituent containing O–S(O)2–NH4. There are also several reaction arrows and labeled H in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring arrows and excluding all bonds involving hydrogen. Reasoning: Count non-hydrogen bonds by region. In the fused hydrocarbon skeleton, the benzene ring has 6 C–C connections; the second six-membered ring shares one fused edge with the benzene ring, so it only additionally contributes 5 C–C connections, totaling 11. The external C=N bond at the upper right counts as 1. The C–O bond from the lower ring carbon to the substituent oxygen counts as 1. The OSO2NH4 fragment includes 1 O–S, two S–O bonds, and 1 S–N, totaling 4. Total = 11 + 1 + 1 + 4 = 17.

raw_record.question_text:
<image_1> In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: Count non-H bonds region by region. First count the fused hydrocarbon framework: the benzene ring contributes 6 C-C connections, and the fused second six-membered ring contributes 5 additional C-C connections because the shared fused edge is not counted twice, giving 11 C-C bonds. Then add the exocyclic C=N bond to NH2+ on the upper right: +1. Add the C-O bond from the lower ring carbon to the substituent: +1. Parse the OSO2NH4 group as O-S, two S-O bonds, and S-N: +4. Total = 11 + 1 + 1 + 4 = 17.
